items.check: Every non-obvious choice the plan makes is logged as a DL-325..DL-334 decision with its own reasoning chain, and no choice appears only inside a milestone's behavior prose
The decision to name the new module traktor_nml/metadata_tier.py and to re-export _TRACKED_ATTRS from splice.py is logged (DL-326) rather than asserted only in CI-M-001-001
The choice to emit a SettledRow on SpliceResult rather than reusing ConflictRow is logged (DL-329) and names the conflict_model projection as the reason
The plan logs an explicit decision for the two items the constraints demand be settled rather than implied: a bound on draw() (DL-332) and reconnect_timeout (DL-333)

OUTLIER_BAND = 0.01 is backed by the user's measured survivor curve (7,279 / 2,679 / 2,203 / 2,180 / 2,176) rather than being a policy default the planner chose, and the boundary case (a gap exactly at 1%) is stated as excluded

The assumption that the tier does not change which record's measured values reach the output is validated against the actual resolution path (_resolve_conflicts patching base's ENTRY span only for a named non-base record, whole-span transplant otherwise), with that citation in the reasoning
The baseline-parity assumption is validated by naming the twelve recorded cases and stating that none invokes splice, rather than assuming manifest.json is unaffected
The mixed-group rule states unambiguously what attrs holds, that such a group produces no settled row, and that it therefore cannot be an outlier - the question the context's assumptions raised
No milestone is an orphan: each of M-001..M-005 carries at least one code_intent, M-005 included as a documentation-only milestone
Every decision_ref resolves to a decision that exists, and every decision DL-325..DL-334 is referenced by at least one code_intent
CI-M-004-003 cites DL-332, a decision that puts a draw() bound OUT of scope; verify the reference is apt for a render intent or is replaced by the decision that actually governs it
No node in DIAG-001 has zero edges
Every edge in DIAG-001 references node ids that exist in its nodes list
Every milestone id named in waves W-001..W-004 exists in milestones, and every milestone appears in exactly one wave
Wave ordering respects the real dependency: M-002 and M-003 both read SpliceResult.settled_rows introduced in M-001, and M-004 places what M-003 composes

readme_entries is empty while M-005 mints DL-325 through DL-334 into traktor_nml/README.md - verify the ten log entries are carried where the executing milestone can read them, or that their absence is deliberate

Every constraint in the task spec is carried into planning_context.constraints with no loss: the DL-307 high-water mark, DL-069, DL-071/DL-079, DL-148/DL-215, DL-084 as amended by DL-169, the fail-first guard rule, the line-ending map, the system interpreter, the MUST-NOTs, and the matching.py/confidence.py exclusion

The DL-084/DL-169 served-page-record constraint is discharged by the milestone that changes a screen: M-004 names both the docs record and its registration in tests/test_docs_browser_record_structure.py
The DL-069 nicegui boundary holds across the plan: metadata_tier.py, splice.py and gui/reconstruct_report.py carry every decision rule, and no rule, band or count lives in app.py
Every risk R-001..R-005 carries a mitigation, an anchor and a decision_ref, and no risk is identified without a stated response

The test-migration risk is discharged by a milestone that owns it: M-001 lists tests/test_splice.py and its acceptance criteria cover both sides of the tier, so the migration is planned work rather than a surprise during execution
The non-numeric or absent measured-value risk has a home in a code_intent (CI-M-001-002 answering no reading rather than raising) and a guard in M-001's error tests

The task spec's 'CLI reconstruct command' is reconciled with the codebase: the plan states no reconstruct subcommand exists and routes the printed reading to commands/splice_cmd.py (M-002) and the page to gui/reconstruct_report.py (M-003)
Reasoning chains are not shallow: each of DL-325..DL-334 states premise, implication and conclusion rather than a bare assertion

Every alternative the user's context named (band-as-rule, tier-plain, keep-playtime-conflicting, paginate the table, widen reconnect_timeout) appears with a rejection reason and a decision_ref, and the withdrawn-on-measurement first choice is recorded as withdrawn rather than as never considered

The contrast between this tier and matching.py's tolerant verification - same-looking idea, different question, no shared tolerance - is captured in invisible_knowledge AND carried into a decision entry so it survives into the log
The LOCATION-is-identity invariant is recorded, including that a re-encode to a new extension is a dangling entry rather than a conflict, so the new rule is never documented as covering that case
The plan records the price it accepts: a settled group inside the band is never named, and the freeze is expected to go with the rows rather than being fixed directly

The user-visible playtime_float exposure (6 groups beyond 1%, worst 3,516s) and the fact that the outlier listing was accepted INSTEAD of keeping playtime conflicting is recorded, so a later reader cannot drop the listing as decoration

The task spec named the Resolve surface, gui/conflict_model.py and the reconnect-wizard artboards as in scope, yet the plan leaves conflict_model and Resolve.dc.html unchanged - verify that exclusion rests on a logged decision rather than an omission
Each milestone's acceptance criteria are observable statements about the built thing rather than restatements of its requirements
The documentation-only milestone claims no guards; verify every behaviour it describes is guarded in M-001..M-004, so 'no guards' is a consequence rather than a gap
Naming is consistent across the plan: settled row, settled_rows, groups_settled_by_rule, settled_groups_outlying, and OUTLIER_BAND against the prose '1%', are used the same way everywhere
The overview's problem and approach agree with the decisions beneath them, and every figure it quotes traces to the measured context rather than being introduced here
